memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So she let them down by a rope through the window, for the house she lived in was part of the city wall. She said to them, "Go to the hills so the pursuers will not find you. Hide yourselves there three days until they return, and then go on your way." — Josh 2:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rahab's home was built into the very wall of Jericho — the wall that would soon come crashing down. From her window she lowers the spies by a rope to safety and gives them wise counsel on how to escape the search parties. Once again we see her faith at work: she does not merely believe, she takes real risks to act on that belief.

There is a striking detail here. Rahab lived in the wall that was doomed to fall, yet within that condemned wall she found safety through her faith. The city around her was under judgment, but she and her household would be spared. She was living, quite literally, in a place of coming destruction, and yet grace would reach her there.

Is that not a picture of every believer? We live in a world under judgment, a world that will one day pass away (2 Pet 3:10). Yet within it, those who trust God are marked out for salvation. We are in the world but not swept away with it, kept safe by grace.

The rope from the window recalls how faith often lowers us out of danger by trusting God's way of escape. Rahab could not save herself by staying comfortable; she had to act. Salvation is God's gift, but it takes hold of us and moves us to respond.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Rahab acted on her faith, not just believed quietly — where is God asking you to act?
2. How does it comfort you that grace reached Rahab even in a "condemned wall"?
3. Are you living as one kept safe by grace within a passing world?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your grace reaches me even in a world under judgment. Give me faith that acts, and keep me safe in You. Amen.
